capabilities.target: Chat reply to the authenticated requester

inputs.source: Employee question submitted via chat, SSO authenticated
Engineering design docs content returned by docs.search; confidential; write access restricted to engineers
Jira ticket content via planned Jira MCP server, including tickets filed by customers

instructions.note: The only control against leaking secrets/credentials is a prompt instruction. It is behavioral and dependent, and it only covers literal secrets/credentials, not confidential design-doc content more broadly.
Any authenticated employee can ask about any engineering design doc docs.search returns; there is no stated role or need-to-know restriction narrower than 'engineering questions'.

elements.name: Arbitrary external web destination reachable via planned web.fetch tool

controls.name: Reply destination bound to authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: The destination is the authenticated requester from the chat session record, not a model-chosen address, and the chat client does not render images or follow links, so there is no path for the model to redirect output elsewhere.

controls.name: Least-privilege, read-only credential for docs.search
controls.decay_rationale: Credential is read-only, so even full model cooperation with an attacker cannot write, delete, or alter design docs through this capability.

controls.name: No egress-capable tool exists today
controls.decay_rationale: There is currently no capability that can move data to an attacker-reachable destination (no web fetch, no link/image rendering). This is why today's path is contained. It fails the moment an egress-capable tool such as web.fetch is added.

controls.name: Prompt instruction forbidding secrets/credentials in answers
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply. A more capable or longer-running model can rationalize exceptions or be steered by injected content into believing an exception applies.

controls.name: Only engineers can write to design docs
controls.decay_rationale: Write access is restricted at the document platform, independent of the model, which is why design-doc content is classified as internal (I) rather than untrusted (U).

controls.name: Network egress allowlist restricting web.fetch to non-attacker-writable destinations
controls.decay_rationale: Would sever exfiltration via web.fetch if destinations cannot be chosen by the model or influenced by untrusted ticket content.

controls.name: Treat Jira ticket content as untrusted and isolate it from tool-argument construction
controls.decay_rationale: Provenance tagging of customer-authored ticket text reduces, but does not eliminate, the chance it is read as instructions; a sufficiently capable model can still be steered by untrusted content embedded in a data field.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action) before web.fetch calls built from retrieved document content
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate reviewing the literal destination URL would block exfiltration attempts regardless of model capability.

findings.title: Confidential design-doc content reaches the chat reply, but destination binding, read-only scope, and the absence of any egress tool keep the path contained today

attack_path.note: Authenticated employee asks an engineering question.
Agent performs a read-only search over confidential design docs.
Agent replies with cited content; the reply is bound to the authenticated requester, and the chat client does not render links or images, so there is no egress channel today.

evidence.observation: 'Replies go only to the authenticated requester. The chat client does not render images or fetch links.' confirms a destination-confirmation control and the absence of a rendering-based egress channel.
'There is no network egress today. The credential is read only.' confirms no egress-capable tool exists and docs_search uses a least-privilege, read-only credential.
'The design docs are confidential. Only engineers can write to them.' supports classifying in.design_docs as internal (I) trust and confidential data_sensitivity.

recommendations.action: Log which documents are returned to which employees so the existing read scope can be audited against need-to-know before docs.search access is ever broadened.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) opens once web.fetch and the customer-facing Jira MCP server are added: customer-authored ticket content could direct the agent to exfiltrate confidential design-doc content via a crafted fetch URL

attack_path.note: Customer-filed Jira ticket content enters context once the Jira MCP server is connected; customers are an untrusted, outside-the-organization source.
Agent reads confidential design docs in the same or an adjacent turn.
Planned tool fetches an external URL; a crafted URL can carry confidential doc content in its query string to an attacker-reachable destination.

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest diff showing a new web.fetch (or equivalent URL-fetch) tool, or a new MCP client config entry for a Jira server; watch especially whether that Jira server's scope includes customer-filed tickets.

evidence.observation: Roadmap note: 'add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references, and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers.' Both are declared as planned, not yet built (cap.web_fetch and in.jira_tickets are marked planned: true).
'There is no network egress today' shows the only reason this path is not live is the absence of an egress tool (ctl.no_egress_capability), which the new_tool trigger directly removes.

The only behavioral instruction ('Never paste secrets or credentials into answers') is scoped to literal secrets/credentials, not to confidential design-doc content in general, so it gives no credit against this path.

recommendations.action: Before shipping web.fetch, restrict it to an allowlist of destinations that cannot be influenced by model output or ticket content, or require a raw-action human approval gate on any URL constructed from retrieved document content.

Before connecting the Jira MCP server, tag customer-filed ticket content as untrusted and keep it out of the context used to construct web.fetch arguments, isolating it from docs_search results read in the same turn.
Log every web.fetch destination together with the triggering input and the document set read in the same turn, so exfiltration attempts are attributable.

governance_refs.note: new_tool and new_mcp_server are significant-change triggers requiring reassessment before launch.

rating.rationale: Today the design is well-contained: docs.search uses a least-privilege read-only credential, replies are bound to the authenticated requester with no link or image rendering, and no egress-capable tool exists, so the only present-day finding (F1) scores low inherent and residual risk. However, the roadmap explicitly plans to add a web.fetch tool and a Jira MCP server that includes customer-filed tickets. Together these would complete a lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted customer ticket content, a read of confidential design docs, and a new egress channel (web.fetch, which can carry data out via a crafted URL). No currently declared control covers either planned capability, so the forecast finding (F2) projects to critical under the new_tool and new_mcp_server triggers, which defeat the one control (ctl.no_egress_capability) responsible for today's low rating. This should be treated as a mandatory pre-launch reassessment point (ISO/IEC 42001 8.2), not a routine feature addition.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; capability scope for docs.search and the planned web.fetch/Jira tools is inferred from prose, so confidence on exact scopes is medium at best.

The planned web.fetch tool and Jira MCP server are roadmap items, not yet built. Finding F2 is conditional on their being built substantially as described; if they are built with materially different scoping (for example, an egress allowlist on web.fetch, or a Jira connector limited to internal tickets only), this forecast must be rerun before launch.
